html:
A small Buddhist temple in Hanoi, Vietnam, built in 1049 as a wooden shrine set on a single stone pillar in a square pond, so that it looks like a lotus flower rising from the water.

The story goes that Emperor Lý Thái Tông, who had no son, dreamed that the bodhisattva Guanyin, seated on a lotus, handed him a baby boy. Soon after he married a peasant girl who bore him a son, and he built the temple in thanks. It stood near the royal citadel of Thăng Long, the capital the Lý dynasty had founded in 1010, and it was rebuilt several times over the centuries.

The kingdom of Đại Việt was then building its own institutions after a thousand years of Chinese rule; the Temple of Literature followed in 1070. French troops blew up the pagoda in 1954 as they withdrew from Hanoi, and it was rebuilt the next year. It stands close to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and is a symbol of the city.
sum: A small Buddhist temple in Hanoi, Vietnam, built in 1049 as a wooden shrine set on a single stone pillar in a square pond, so that it looks like a lotus flower rising from the water.
